extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for machine unlearning consisting of 200 diverse synthetic fictitious author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, plus forget/retain splits and evaluation datasets for assessing unlearning efficacy in large language models.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini; Zhili Feng; Avi Schwarzschild; Zachary C. Lipton; J. Zico Kolter
extraction.citeAs: Maini, Pratyush; Feng, Zhili; Schwarzschild, Avi; Lipton, Zachary C.; Kolter, J. Zico. TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121v1, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated as fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4. The authors prompted GPT-4 with predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, genre, awards, parents' professions, and book-title seeds, and asked it to generate 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author. The final dataset contains 200 synthetic author profiles. The benchmark also defines forget and retain subsets with 99-1, 95-5, and 90-10 splits, and includes additional evaluation datasets called Real Authors and World Facts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data consists of GPT-4-generated fictitious author biographies and question-answer pairs. Seed attributes were provided in prompts, and book-title keywords were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors iterated on prompting to reduce confounders and pretraining leakage. An initial raw dataset of 50 authors created with a generic prompt showed repeated words and biased patterns. They then used a more elaborate prompt that deterministically seeded author attributes such as place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, parents' occupations, and words in book titles. Keywords for book titles were randomly selected from two books from each genre in the Goodreads Books dataset to increase diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was brought into final form by prompting GPT-4 to return content strictly as 20 question-answer pairs per author, with detailed and self-contained answers and the author's full name appearing in each question. The benchmark was then split into forget and retain sets at 99-1, 95-5, and 90-10 ratios. Additional evaluation datasets were constructed: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts. For evaluation, paraphrased answers and five factually incorrect perturbations per answer were also generated with GPT-4.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations/labels were generated synthetically rather than by human annotators. GPT-4 authored the fictitious biographies and the 20 question-answer pairs for each author. For evaluation, GPT-4 was also used to paraphrase answers and generate five factually incorrect perturbed answers for truth-ratio computation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes generation bias in an initial raw 50-author dataset and compares word frequencies between the raw and final prompted versions, finding that seeding attributes is critical to avoid repeated patterns such as words like 'tides' and 'shadows'. The authors state this was done to minimize confounders leaking from pretraining data and to create a clean unlearning setup with controlled sources of information.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author profile
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The prompt seeds include attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, gender orientation, parents' professions, and writing genre. The paper emphasizes that all author data is entirely fabricated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by privacy and legal concerns around large language models memorizing and reproducing sensitive or private data, including the Right to be Forgotten. The authors argue that better unlearning methods are critical for building more secure and trustworthy systems and for safe, and in some places legal, deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Because the biographies are generated using GPT-4, the authors explicitly consider the risk that generated data may leak biases from pretraining data. In an initial raw dataset made with a generic prompt, they observed biased patterns: most birth years clustered between 1970 and 1980, especially August 1975; many book titles reused words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', and 'whispers'; and many authors had similar upbringings and 'magical' writing styles. They mitigated this by deterministically seeding attributes in the prompt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only studies entity-level unlearning and leaves out instance-level unlearning, behavior-level unlearning, and in-context unlearning. It is designed around information learned during finetuning rather than pretraining, which the authors note is a limitation by design for accessibility and control. The benchmark provides exact forget and retain sets, so it does not address the challenge of discovering them in real-world settings. The forget-quality metric is an approximation of indistinguishability and can rate gibberish-producing models as having strong forget quality, so it must be paired with model utility. The benchmarked unlearning methods are limited to simple baselines, and the linear-compute constraint may not be optimal.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for finetuning base LLMs on fictitious author question answering and then evaluating machine unlearning methods. It supports training/finetuning on the full TOFU dataset, unlearning on designated forget sets, and evaluation on Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts. It is designed to study unlearning efficacy, privacy-preserving model modification, and the trade-off between forget quality and model utility.
